primary.title: Studies on Fermentation: The Diseases of Beer, Their Causes, and the Means of Preventing Them
primary.author: Louis Pasteur
primary.rationale: A foundational work by Pasteur detailing his research into fermentation, a key area of his scientific contributions. It's likely to be available in digitized historical scientific collections.

primary.title: Pasteur's Scientific Papers
primary.author: Louis Pasteur
primary.rationale: A collection of Pasteur's most significant scientific papers, offering direct insight into his discoveries and methodologies. Such collected works are often digitized.

primary.title: The Germ Theory of Disease
primary.author: Louis Pasteur
primary.rationale: This refers to a lecture or paper where Pasteur articulated his groundbreaking germ theory of disease. His major lectures and papers are often preserved and digitized.

secondary.title: Pasteur: The Man and His Work
secondary.author: René Dubos
secondary.rationale: A highly regarded biography by a prominent microbiologist, offering a comprehensive and scholarly analysis of Pasteur's life and scientific achievements.

secondary.title: Louis Pasteur: A Life
secondary.author: Gerald L. Geison
secondary.rationale: A definitive and critically acclaimed biography that delves deeply into Pasteur's scientific work, personal life, and the historical context of his discoveries.

secondary.title: The Pasteur Revolution: How the French Scientist Changed the Way We Think About Medicine
secondary.author: E. Richard Brown
secondary.rationale: This book examines the profound impact of Pasteur's work on the development of modern medicine and public health, providing a scholarly perspective.

suggestions.notes: Primary source availability on Wikisource and Project Gutenberg is less certain for specific scientific treatises compared to Internet Archive, which often hosts older scientific literature. Secondary sources are chosen for their scholarly reputation and recency.
